text: By government decision, legislative changes will be prepared regarding the recognition of diplomas issued before 2010.

By decision of the Government of Georgia, legislative changes will be submitted to Parliament, based on which problems related to the recognition of diplomas issued before 2010 will be resolved for thousands of citizens – stated Givi Mikanadze, the Minister of Education, Science, and Youth of Georgia.
As the minister noted, according to the amendment, 4-year full-time and 5-year part-time studies will be recognized equally.

According to him/her, the change will affect students who were enrolled in the university under a recognized status and completed their studies under an unrecognized status, as well as citizens who were enrolled in the university by educational institutions before they obtained a license.

"We had the following situation: our citizens in 4-year programs were taking exactly the same number of subjects and receiving the same qualification as those in 5-year distance learning programs. According to the legislation in place until now, the 5-year program was equated to a Master’s degree, while the 4-year program was awarded a Bachelor’s degree. Based on the changes, those who completed a 4-year program will receive a diploma equivalent to a Master’s degree, which will significantly facilitate the employment of citizens in their desired fields."

Before 2010, until a unified system was established, there was no registry in the field of education to ensure that students were kept informed. There were cases where specific universities that had not been granted accreditation failed to inform applicants and enrolled them anyway. Subsequently, when diplomas were issued, graduates faced problems regarding the recognition of these documents.

Furthermore, a number of higher education institutions were authorized for a certain period, but their authorization was revoked during the period of study. Students were not informed about this either, and subsequently, these graduates faced problems.

"The proposed legislative changes will finally put an end to the lengthy and problematic processes our citizens undergo for diploma recognition—going to court and appealing decisions, which involve significant time and effort. All of this will become a thing of the past once and for all, and the diplomas of thousands of our citizens will be recognized," stated Givi Mikanadze.
